composition.story: Bayesian optimization has measured three settings. It fits a surrogate model that predicts a score and its uncertainty everywhere. An acquisition score combines both. The next setting to try is the acquisition peak, which is not always the best predicted score.

aha.observation: The next setting is the acquisition peak at 0.70. Its mean is lower than at 0.35, but its uncertainty is much larger.

states.label: Observed
states.sentence: Three settings have been tried and scored. Nothing is known about the settings between them.
states.why: The model can only learn from measured trials.

states.label: Fit surrogate
states.sentence: A surrogate model is fitted to the trials. It predicts a mean score for every setting.
states.why: Predictions are cheap, so many settings can be compared without running trials.

states.label: Add uncertainty
states.sentence: The model also reports uncertainty. It is small near measured trials and large in the unexplored gap.
states.why: A wide band means the true score could be much higher or lower.

states.label: Score options
states.sentence: The acquisition score adds mean and uncertainty at each setting. High values mean promising or poorly known.
states.why: One number now balances exploiting good results and exploring gaps.

states.label: Pick next
states.sentence: The next trial is the acquisition peak, 0.70. It beats 0.35 despite a lower predicted mean.
states.why: Large uncertainty gives 0.70 more potential gain than the known good region.

7.reason: At brief depth the states build up one idea at a time with only two readouts each and a single callout target, so it stays uncluttered, with up to three active regions in the middle steps.
